source_title: GBrain — Garry's Opinionated OpenClaw/Hermes Agent Brain

discovered_urls.context: OpenClaw is the primary agent runtime gbrain is built to plug into; gbrain declares `bundle-plugin` with `openclaw.compat.pluginApi: '>=2026.4.0'`; README prescribes AlphaClaw on Render as the default agent host
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 9/10 — OpenClaw has appeared in our catalogue via openclaw/acpx but the website and the core runtime (AlphaClaw) have not been ingested directly; very likely the anchor of a whole ecosystem

discovered_urls.context: One-click Render deploy for AlphaClaw, the recommended OpenClaw runtime for installing gbrain; directly referenced in the README's 'Need an AI agent first?' block
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 9/10 — the default agent host that gbrain ships against; we should catalogue AlphaClaw alongside gbrain since they are architectural pair

discovered_urls.context: The other agent runtime gbrain is built to plug into; already referenced by our Hermes-Wiki entry but the core hermes-agent repo itself has not been directly ingested
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 8/10 — Hermes Agent underlies Hermes-Wiki (already catalogued); the core runtime is worth a direct entry for completeness of the 'Hermes family' cluster

discovered_urls.context: Railway one-click deploy template for Hermes Agent referenced in gbrain README's Need-an-Agent-First block
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 6/10 — useful deploy template if we want to trial Hermes Agent ourselves; minor but operationally handy

discovered_urls.context: Explicit architecture essay articulating the 'thin binary, fat markdown skill' philosophy — the clearest external match to our own L-Thread architecture we have seen
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 10/10 — ready-to-cite language for client pitches and meeting-prep; should be lifted into an internal design doc

discovered_urls.context: Companion essay framing integration recipes as 'Homebrew for personal AI' — same philosophical argument for why markdown is the install medium
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 9/10 — directly adoptable framing for any tool that ships installable recipes

discovered_urls.context: The 'most important doc in the repo' per the README — full production agent playbook: brain-agent loop, entity detection, enrichment pipeline, meeting ingestion, reference cron schedule
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 9/10 — template for our own L-Thread skill pack; contains the 7-step copy-paste GOAL block we should mirror

discovered_urls.context: Brain repo directory structure: MECE directories (people/, companies/, deals/, concepts/, etc.) with README.md resolvers in each
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 7/10 — schema template we could adapt to our practitioner/project ontology

discovered_urls.context: 10-star vision doc for the integration system — likely contains the long-form argument for why recipes are Homebrew formulas
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 7/10 — vision framing; useful for long-form thinking about integration marketplaces

discovered_urls.context: Embedded Postgres 17.5 via WASM; powers gbrain's zero-config default mode; 2-second boot, real Postgres + pgvector + pg_trgm in a single-process WASM runtime
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 9/10 — this is a general-purpose primitive that could replace our JSON-in-git state store for L-Thread dev mode; direct candidate for catalogue entry as infrastructure

discovered_urls.context: 15KB CLAUDE.md with ship workflow, E2E test DB lifecycle, community PR wave process, skill routing rules — worth studying as an example of a production project CLAUDE.md
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 8/10 — our own orchestrator CLAUDE.md is lighter; this is a strong reference for what a mature project file looks like

discovered_urls.context: 25KB changelog with explicit 'voice guidance' in CLAUDE.md: 'write changelog entries that sell the upgrade, not document the implementation'; example of agent-readable changelog pattern
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 7/10 — worth borrowing the voice-guidance approach for our orchestrator CHANGELOG

discovered_urls.context: 7 integration recipes as markdown files: twilio-voice-brain, email-to-brain, x-to-brain, calendar-to-brain, meeting-sync, ngrok-tunnel, credential-gateway — each with dependency resolution
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 8/10 — recipe format is a strong template for agent-installable integrations; especially x-to-brain which matches our own X-activity ingest flow

discovered_urls.context: Model routing table for sub-agents — gbrain's own take on which model to use for which skill
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 8/10 — directly adjacent to our 'Opus-only feedback' and L-Thread model routing decisions

discovered_urls.context: Two-repo pattern (agent vs brain) — architectural separation between the harness code repo and the knowledge repo
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 7/10 — validates our own orchestrator/ + catalogue/ separation pattern

discovered_urls.context: Cron/watch/webhook options for live brain sync from git repo to indexed backend — directly relevant if we ever wire our catalogue to auto-sync
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 7/10 — operational playbook for git-to-index sync pattern

discovered_urls.context: Pluggable engine interface documentation: PGLite (default) + Postgres, capability matrix, migration path
discovered_urls.relevance_hint: 8/10 — reference for how to architect a pluggable-backend system in our own state store
